newsitem.title: GERMANY: Traders welcome German retail coffee price rises.
newsitem.headline: Traders welcome German retail coffee price rises.

text.p: Plans by German coffee roasters to raise retail prices by March 10 were welcomed on Monday by traders struggling to secure supplies in a tight market.
"The moves will create more liquidity, but they may even be too little, too late," one said.
"But at least we hope the industry will be better able to finance the enormous holding costs involved this year."
Roasters have been buying hand to mouth for months in a bid to reconcile low retail prices and rising costs.
Some were caught out by rallies towards 150 cents per lb by New York forward arabica positions, where origin fixing has reportedly taken place in a 110 and 120 cents range.

Kraft Jacobs Suchard, which took the lead in Germany last Friday to announce price rises of one mark per 0.5 kilos, said high quality arabicas cost 45 percent more than last December and the dollar had risen by 10 percent since then.
Tied-outlet roaster Tchibo earlier on Monday said it would increase prices on some 60 percent of its products by 0.50 marks per 0.5 kilos from February 27.
Traders said consumers would go along with the higher prices after some initial hoarding, and industry association DKV shared this view.
"Retail levels are very low and the price increases are relatively modest -- we expect shoppers will absorb them," said DKV managing director Frieder Rotzoll.
Fundamentals were looking very tight for 1997 and beyond, with Brazil's crop the main uncertainty and with low consumer stocks generating demand, traders added.
They were concerned by forecasts that the Brazilian crop for delivery in the second half of 1997 might fall well below the 26 million produced last year.
Fuelled by concern over tightness, New York March last Friday ended up 0.25 cents at 151.25 cents a lb and May at 146.00, up 1.20.
The contract looks poised for further gains on the threatened national strike in Colombia on Tuesday.
In the northern German import market, buyers were keenly seeking Brazils and Central Americans and were also showing interest in African and Indian arabicas.
Arabicas rose by $11-13 per 50 kg on the week, with Brazils up $11 at $168 fob ex-origin. Second hand cost $157.
Vietnam robustas were at $71 cif for February, up $5.
